assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and realised to uncertainties near 1e-18 by Ye's group, redefined what precision measurement can reach. It is a clear, original idea whose consequences span metrology, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy. From an atomic-structure standpoint the physics (magic wavelengths, clock-transition shifts, many-body control of lattice atoms) is clean and well understood.
assessment.attribution: Two names carry the decisive contributions: Katori proposed and first demonstrated the lattice-clock concept, and Ye's group pushed it to the leading accuracy and stability and added the many-body and cavity-comb connections. The credited list supports a compact, fair two-person prize. Other contributors (for example, ion-clock and comb communities) are recognised elsewhere, so some allocation debate remains, but I would not call it unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have reproduced and surpassed the early results over two decades, and a redefinition of the second is under discussion. Timing is good, perhaps overdue given the 2005 and 2012 prizes on adjacent topics.
uncertainties: I rely on my own recollection of the clock-accuracy milestones and have not verified specific numbers.
Whether the committee would prefer to bundle ion clocks or the comb into the same recognition is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new platform for strongly correlated physics: flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity tuned by twist angle. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted the magic angle, and the 2018 experiments confirmed the correlated behaviour. The impact on condensed-matter research has been very large and fast.
assessment.attribution: The theory-experiment pairing is natural: Bistritzer and MacDonald for the prediction, Jarillo-Herrero for the decisive experiments. Cao et al. had other co-authors, and Dean and Kim also contributed to the moire platform, so credit around the experiment is not fully clean, but the supplied names support a three-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across many groups is strong, but the mechanism of superconductivity and the nature of the correlated states are still debated, so the interpretation is not fully settled. Recognition now is plausible but may be a few years early.
uncertainties: The origin of superconductivity in twisted graphene is unresolved.
Allocation among moire-platform contributors beyond the three names may be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall state from spin-orbit coupling and its experimental realisation in HgTe wells launched the field of topological insulators. The concept is original, clean, and has had lasting influence on materials, spintronics proposals and the study of topological phases.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the original theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group made the decisive experimental observation following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The credited names give a coherent trio, but Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (and Fu for the 3D case) are not available in this entry, so the allocation is imperfect and arguably incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation in 2D and 3D materials is extensive and independent, and the framework is stable after nearly two decades. Timing is mature, although the 2016 prize touched topological phases.
uncertainties: Omitted contributors (3D topological insulators, the HgTe proposal) could make this trio contested.
Overlap with the 2016 topological-phase recognition may weigh against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal showed how to build quantum gates with trapped ions, and Blatt's group demonstrated gates and algorithms in practice. This links atomic physics directly to quantum computing, with lasting influence. The atomic-physics foundations (motional modes, laser-ion coupling) are well established.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the theoretical proposal; Blatt led key experimental implementations, though Wineland (already a laureate) and others also contributed to the ion-trap gate toolbox. The trio is a plausible configuration, with some ambiguity over experimental credit.
assessment.maturity: Trapped-ion processors are demonstrated by several groups and companies, so confirmation is strong. Quantum information was recognised in 2022, which may reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 and 2022 prizes could make a further quantum-information award less likely.
Experimental credit relative to other ion-trap groups is not fully resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP's full-sky CMB maps fixed the cosmological parameters to a few percent and established the precision era of cosmology. The impact is large and its measurements are foundational for the standard model of cosmology.
assessment.attribution: WMAP was a large collaboration; Bennett as principal investigator, Page as instrument builder and Spergel for the analysis form a reasonable trio. Credit relative to COBE (2006 prize) and Planck remains a question, and mission credit always involves many people.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed by Planck and by other probes. The results are mature, though the 2006 and 2019 prizes already recognised parts of the CMB and cosmology programme.
uncertainties: A prize for WMAP might be seen as overlapping with COBE and the 2019 cosmology prize.
Allocation within a large mission team is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gives a controlled non-perturbative treatment of local correlations and has become a standard tool for Mott physics and correlated materials. Its conceptual clarity comes from the infinite-dimension limit. From my many-body background I value the method as a real step beyond perturbative approaches.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimensional limit, while Georges and Kotliar built the mapping onto an impurity model. The credited trio includes Vollhardt but not Metzner, and Kotliar and Georges' contribution is decisive, so allocation is reasonably supported but not perfectly complete.
assessment.maturity: The method has been widely adopted for decades with many material applications, though its quantitative reliability for low-dimensional systems is limited. Timing is mature.
uncertainties: Metzner's role in the original formulation is missing from the credited names.
Methodological prizes are less common and the committee may prefer a discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and was an enormous experimental achievement in detector technology and analysis. It is clearly worthy in scientific terms.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised the theory; the experimental credit lies with two collaborations of thousands. The listed names are founding leaders of the projects, which supports a fair configuration but not a unique one. The committee has traditionally resisted large-collaboration prizes, and credit is hard to resolve.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by two independent experiments and subsequent measurements; timing is fully mature.
uncertainties: Attribution within ATLAS and CMS is inherently contested.
I rely on memory of the project leadership roles, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution links the foundations of quantum mechanics to secure communication, and its importance for quantum information is substantial. BB84 and E91 are original and conceptually clear.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the BB84 originators and Ekert introduced the entanglement-based protocol, so the trio is a reasonable configuration. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is a possible historical complication.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally demonstrated for decades, with commercial systems, though practical security under realistic devices is still being refined. The 2022 prize on entanglement and Bell tests partially covers the field.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize may reduce its chance.
